THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:4.1.2012 PASSED IN MVC NO.19/2011 ON THE FILE OF SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE & MEMBER,
ADDITIONAL MACT, HIRIYUR, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for short), seeking enhancement of the compensation.

2. The undisputed facts are that the claimant has sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 12.09.2010 at about 6.30 a.m., near bus stand of Shravanagere Village on Dharmapura-Hiriyur Road when motorcycle bearing No.KA-16/Q-9036 dashed against the claimant.
Therefore, the claimant has filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
4.
The Tribunal has granted the compensation under various heads as follows:
Sl . No

. Particulars Amount (in.Rs.)
1. Towards Pain and Sufferings 20,000.00 2.
Towards Attendant Charges 3,500.00 3. Towards Medical Expenses 54,165.00 4.
Towards Future Medical 10,000.00 Expenses 5.
Towards loss of earnings due 81,000.00 to disability Total 1,68,665.00 5.
In the present case, from the medical evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant has sustained fracture of left femur.
The claimant is an agriculturist.

Therefore, considering the nature Sri Sannamallappa vs Sri. R. Lokesha on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179852667/

sentences.text: of injuries sustained, the compensation awarded under the head 'Pain and Suffering' is on the lesser side.

Therefore, the same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/-.
6.
Further, the compensation granted under the head 'medical expenses' is as per the actual medical bills produced by the claimant.
Therefore, the same is kept in tact.

7. The doctor has assessed that the claimant has suffered 60% of permanent physical disability towards left lower limb and for whole body, it would be 20% of functional disability affecting earning capacity but the Tribunal has taken only 15%.
Therefore, it is held as 20% functional disability.
The accident was occurred in the year 2010.
Therefore, the notional income would be Rs.5,500/-.
As the claimant was aged 40 years, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '15'.

Hence,
the 'loss of future income due to disability' is hereby re-

assessed and quantified as under:
Rs.5,500 x 20/100 x 15 x 12 = Rs.1,98,000/-

Accordingly, a sum of Rs.1,98,000/- is awarded under the head 'loss of future income due to disability'.
8.
Further, the claimant was an inpatient for a period of 25 days in the hospital.

The claimant being agriculturist, he was needed bed rest at-least for a period of four months and also he might not have attended the work of agriculture during that period and that is to be compensated.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.22,000/- (Rs.5,500 x 4 months) is awarded under the head 'loss of income during laid up period'.
9. The Tribunal has not awarded the compensation under the head 'loss of amenities'.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.35,000/- is awarded under the said head.
10. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.10,000/- under the head 'future medical expenses' which is on the lesser side.
Therefore, the same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/-.
Further, for Incidental expenses like food, nourishment, attendant, etc., a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded.

11. Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the following sums:
Sl.

No . Particulars Compensation awarded (in Rs.)
1. Towards Pain and Sufferings 40,000.00 2. Towards incidental expenses 25,000.00 like food, nourishment, conveyance, etc.
3 . Towards Medical Expenses 54,165.00 4. Towards Future Medical 40,000.00 Expenses

5. Towards loss of earnings due 1,98,000.00 to disability Sri Sannamallappa vs Sri. R. Lokesha on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179852667/
3
6 . Loss of income during laid up 22,000.00 period 7. Loss of amenities 35,000.00
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.1,68,665/- but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.4,14,165/-.

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,45,500/- (Rs.4,14,165 - Rs.1,68,665) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

13. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.19/2011 is hereby modified holding the claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,45,500/- with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

iii. 
The claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 86 days in filing the appeal.

iv. Costs made easy.
v. Draw award accordingly.

Sd/-
